Thank you for your email regarding the renewal of our Master Services Agreement ahead of its expiry on 31 October 2026. We value our ongoing partnership and are supportive of renewing for a further 12-month term as provided for under Clause 8.1.

We would ask that this amount be applied against our renewal invoicing.

trace.approvals_confirmed: Finance Director sign-off required before agreeing to the 7% counter-offer, as it exceeds the 5% threshold under Policy Rule 2.; Vendor's written confirmation/agreement to the proposed 7% renewal terms and SLA credit application is required to finalize the deal.; Decision on whether to pursue competitive bidding (Zenith/Orbit quotes) if Acme rejects the 7% counter-offer, including FX re-verification before use.
trace.internal_note:
- Approvals needed: Finance Director sign-off required if we ultimately agree to anything above 5% (Policy Rule 2), including our own 7% counter-offer; written justification from vendor should be requested if they push back above 5%.
- Per Policy Rule 3, the vendor's original 12% ask must not be accepted as-is; it has been countered down to the contractual cap of 7% (Clause 8.2), referenced per Policy Rule 5.
- Per Policy Rule 4, the unclaimed SLA credit of Rs 20,000 (May and July shortfalls, Rs 10,000 each) must be claimed before renewal is finalized — this has been included in the message.
- Competitor quotes (Zenith Cloud Pte Ltd at indicative Rs 2,10,804/month with 99.95% SLA, and Orbit Hosting Inc at indicative Rs 2,15,595/month with 99.9% SLA) were not referenced in the vendor-facing message but support our negotiating position; these are converted using a live but unverified FX rate (1 USD = 95.82 INR, dated 2026-09-25) and should be re-checked before being relied upon internally or used in further negotiation.
- If Acme rejects the 7% counter, next step per Policy Rule 3 is to consider competitive bidding using the Zenith/Orbit quotes as reference points (after FX re-verification).
- Major incident details (3 total: two in May, one in July) were not included in the vendor-facing message, as a matter of standard practice — this operational detail is not necessary to support the SLA credit claim or the price negotiation.
